Rare, then, is the one who despises the small days of this world and thinks royal power worth nothing. When we see the powerful of the world gleaming with gold, glowing with purple and gems, surrounded by an army, let us say within ourselves: Who, do you think, despises the small days? Hence Jacob too, understanding that the life of men is short: Small, he says, and very evil are the days of my life. Those, then, who have despised the small days — and he refers this to royal power, to admonish Zerubbabel and Joshua and the people building the temple of God, by no means to fear the adversaries who were hindering them, but to listen to the Lord exhorting them — those, from the fact that they despise royal grandeur, shall also rejoice and see the help of the Savior, who is promised from the stock of Zerubbabel, and because […]

As for the seven eyes, which run to and fro through the whole earth and judge all things, we explained above that they are the seven spirits; and that nothing is hidden from the Lord, who is aware of things past and present and to come, and renders to each according to his works, above all when he comes in the person of the one who separates the good and the wicked, and of the refiner.

4:11.t: Of the two olive trees which were on the right of the lamp and on the left we have read above. And so the prophet, now asking about them, does not deserve to hear, because he does not retain the former things; or else because what was said there more obscurely he desires to hear here more plainly; or at any rate his obstinacy is refuted by the angel's silence, because he insists that he knows greater things; although the Hebrews maintain that he heard nothing when he asked about the olive trees for this reason, that he did not ask well, and did not inquire into the whole of what he ought to have known. In short, afterwards he inquires more fully, adding the ears or branches of the olive trees, about which he had been silent above. For there he said: What are these two olive trees? Here he asks: What are the two ears of the olive trees? […]

And I answered, and said to him: What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand, and on its left? And I answered a second time, and said to him: What are the two ears of the olive trees, which are upon the two golden beaks, in which are the pourers of gold? And he said to me, saying: Do you not know what these are? And I said: No, lord. And he said: These are the two sons of oil, who stand by the Ruler of the whole earth. LXX: And I answered, and said to him: What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand, and on the left? And I asked a second time, and said to him: What are the two branches of the olive trees, which are in the hands of the two golden nostrils, which pour in and draw back the golden pourers. And he said to me: Do you not know what these are? And I said: By no means, lord. And he said to me: These are the two sons of fatness, who stand by the Lord of the whole earth. […]

Some of our writers interpret the two olive trees as the Son and the Holy Spirit, and the lamp in the middle as God the Father. But I do not know how, without blasphemy, they can take one as on the right and the other as on the left. The branches, too, or ears of the olive trees, they explain as the incarnation of the Savior and the likeness of a dove of the Holy Spirit, because we cannot see the olive trees whole, but a certain part, and, so to speak, the little branches of the incarnation of Christ and of the manifestation of the Holy Spirit have been shown to us. Others understand the two testaments, the Gospel on the right, the law on the left, because in the one there is the spiritual sense, in the other the bodily; and because we can explain neither the whole Gospel nor the whole law: And now we know in part, and we prophesy in part, and we cannot yet understand what is perfect. […]

4:14.t: "These are the two candlesticks standing before the Lord of the earth." These two candlesticks and two olive trees He has to this end spoken of, and admonished you that if, when you have read of them elsewhere, you have not understood, you may understand here. For in Zechariah, one of the twelve prophets, it is thus written: "These are the two olive trees and two candlesticks which stand in the presence of the Lord of the earth; " that is, they are in paradise. Also, in another sense, standing in the presence of the lord of the earth, that is, in the presence of Antichrist. Therefore they must be slain by Antichrist.
4:14.s: Commentary on the Apocalypse of the Blessed John

5:1.t: And I turned, and lifted up my eyes, and saw, and behold, a flying scroll. And he said to me: What do you see? And I said: I see a flying scroll; its length twenty cubits, and its breadth ten cubits. And he said to me: This is the curse that goes forth over the face of the whole earth, for every thief, as it is written there, shall be judged, and everyone who swears shall likewise be judged by it. I will bring it forth, says the Lord of hosts, and it shall come to the house of the thief, and to the house of him who swears falsely by my name, and it shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it, and its timbers, and its stones. LXX: And I turned, and lifted up my eyes, and saw a flying sickle. And he said to me: What do you see? And I said: I see a flying sickle, of twenty cubits in length, and ten cubits in breadth. […]

5:2.t:
It comes in opportunely today even from the Old Testament to show you the heinousness of perjury. "There was," it says, "a flying sickle, ten cubits in breadth." The "flying" betokens the swift advent of the vengeance which pursues oaths; that it is many cubits in length and breadth, signifies the force and magnitude of the woes; that it comes flying "from heaven," is to show that the vengeance comes from the judgment-seat on high: that it is in the form of a "sickle," denotes the inevitableness of the doom: for just as the sickle, where it comes and has hooked the neck, is not drawn back with nothing but itself, but with the head reaped off, even so the vengeance which comes upon the swearers is severe, and will not desist until it have completed its work.

But if we swear and escape, let us not be confident; this is but to our woe. For what think ye? How many, since Ananias and Sapphira, have dared the same with them? How is it then, say you, that they have not met with the same fate? […]

I have read that the twenty cubits of length and the ten of breadth refer to the age of the Lord Savior, that is, they make the number thirty, because the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, and by him the world is to be judged.

5:3.t: And at the same time let us warn those who think theft and perjury small crimes, that the curse which is described in the scroll and the sickle is brought into the house of the thief and of the perjurer, and remains in it, and consumes all its timbers and stones. But if in these things which are thought lesser — theft, I mean, and perjury — there is so great a threat of punishments, what shall we say of fornication, adultery, homicide, sacrilege, and all the crimes which are numbered by the Apostle among the works of the flesh?

5:5.t: For "now," saith he, "the axe is laid unto the root of the trees." There is nothing more terrible than this turn of his discourse. For it is no longer "a flying sickle," nor "the taking down of a hedge," nor "the treading under foot of the vineyard;" but an axe exceeding sharp, and what is worse, it is even at the doors. For inasmuch as they continually disbelieved the prophets, and used to say, "Where is the day of the Lord?" and "let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, that we may know it," by reason that it was many years before what they said came to pass; to lead them off from this encouragement also, he sets the terrors close to them. And this he declared by saying "now," and by his putting it to "the root." "For the space between is nothing now," saith he, "but it is laid to the very root." And he said not, "to the branches," nor "to the fruits," but "to the root." Signifying, that if they were negligent, they would have incurable horrors to endure, and not have so much as a hope of remedy. […]
5:5.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 3:7.4

5:5.t: The angel who was speaking in the prophet, having gone out from him and speaking as it were face to face, bids him lift up his eyes and see the sins of the people of Israel heaped up into a full measure, and the offences of all filled up; and that this is their eye, which in Hebrew is called enam, and is written with ain, iod, nun, mem. Or their iniquity, which, if it were written with the letter uau, would rightly be read onam, as the LXX rendered; and this error has often crept into the common edition, that because the letters uau and iod are of the same shape but differ in size, one is read for the other. This jar or measure is their eye in the whole earth, that is, the showing of sins, so that those whose vices lay hidden, scattered, might be heaped up into one and laid open to the eyes of all, and Israel might go forth from its place, and it might be shown to all the nations what Israel had been in its own land.

And the angel who was speaking in me went out, and said to me: Lift up your eyes, and see what this is that goes forth. And I said: What is it? And he said: This is a jar going forth; and he said: This is their eye in the whole earth. And behold, a talent of lead was being carried, and behold, a woman was sitting in the midst of the jar. And he said: This is impiety, and he cast her into the midst of the jar, and put a lump of lead into its mouth. LXX: And the angel who was speaking in me went out, and said to me: Look up with your eyes and see what it is that goes forth; and I said: What is it? And he said: This is the measure that goes forth. And he said: This is their iniquity in all the earth. And behold, a talent of lead was lifted up; and behold, a woman was sitting in the midst of the measure, and he said: This is iniquity, and he cast her into the midst of the measure, and cast a stone of lead into its mouth. A jar, or a measure, was going forth and being carried in the air. […]

5:7.t: "They went down into the deep like a stone." Why did "they go down into the deep like a stone"? Because they were not such "stones as those from which sons of Abraham could be raised up," but such as loved the deep and cherished the liquid element — that is, who seized the bitter and fleeting pleasure of present things. Whence it is said of them: "They were sunk like lead in the mightiest water." Sinners are heavy. Finally, iniquity too is shown "to sit upon a talent of lead," as the prophet Zechariah says: "I saw," he says, "a woman sitting upon a talent of lead, and I said: what is this? And he answered: iniquity." Thence it is, therefore, that the wicked "were sunk into the deep, like lead in the mightiest water."

For virtue is a light and buoyant thing, and all who live in her way "fly like clouds," as Isaiah says, "and as doves with their young ones"; but sin is a heavy affair, "sitting," as another of the prophets says, "upon a talent of lead." If, however, this reading of the history appears to any forced and inapplicable, and the miracle at the Red Sea does not present itself to him as written for our profit, let him listen to the Apostle: "Now all these things happened unto them for types, and they are written for our admonition."

The deserts of each one of us are suspended in the balance, which a little weight either of good works or of degenerate conduct sways this way or that; if the evil preponderate, woe is me! if the good, pardon is at hand. For no man is free from sin; but where good preponderates, the evil flies up, is overshadowed, and covered. Wherefore in the Day of judgement our works will either succour us, or will sink us into the deep, weighed down as with a millstone. For iniquity is heavy, supported as by a talent of lead; avarice is intolerable, and all pride is foul dishonesty. Wherefore exhort the people of God to trust rather in the Lord, to abound in the riches of simplicity, wherein they may walk without snare and without hindrance.

And behold, a talent of lead was being carried. For talent of lead we read in what follows stone of lead. A talent is called chachar; a stone, aben. It is, then, the stone of lead which is also the talent of lead, which we, expressing it more plainly, have translated as a lump or ball of lead, by which is signified the very heavy weight of sins.

And upon this measure and jar of all offences sat impiety in the midst, which by another name we can call idolatry, and the denial of God. Hence it is said by the Savior to the Jews: Fill up the measure of your fathers. This impiety, which sat upon the sins of Israel and gloried in its wickedness, is afterwards sent into the midst of Babylon, and is crushed by the evil of captivity. Or, according to Theodotion, she casts herself and hides in the midst of the jar, and draws over herself the very heavy weight of lead, so that she has her mouth stopped and can no longer boast herself. Or else she is crushed by the angel of God, so that she who before rejoiced in wickedness may fall silent in eternal silence. But whither, and by whom, she is carried shut in, the following reading teaches.

5:9.t: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, two women coming out, and the spirit was in their wings, and they had wings like the wings of a kite, and they lifted up the jar between earth and heaven. And I said to the angel who spoke in me: Where are these carrying the jar? And he said to me: That a house may be built for it in the land of Shinar, and that it may be established, and set there upon its base. LXX: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, two women coming out, and the spirit was in their wings, and they had wings as are the wings of a hoopoe. And they lifted up the measure between earth and heaven. And I said to the angel who spoke in me: Where are these carrying the measure? And he said to me: To build a house for it in the land of Babylon, and to prepare it, and to set it there upon its seat. The Jews take the two women coming out to be the kingdom of the Medes and that of the Macedonians, each of which afflicted the Babylonian people, and there their impiety set up its seat. […]

If we choose to take the two women as the peoples of the heretics and of the Jews — both of whom go out from the face of the Lord, and are borne by an unsteady spirit, and have the wings of the kite, the heron and the hoopoe, since, after the manner of the partridge, they are forever gathering riches, and not with judgment, and hasten to snatch from the Church, and delight in contentions and quarrels, and drag to destruction whomever they have deceived, and wallow in the mire of lusts and in everlasting filth —, these women lift up the most heavy weight of impiety, and build their house in confusion, and serve the Babylonian king, so that the peoples of the heretics and of the Jews may dwell there, where the idolaters abide, serving wood and stones.

5:10.t: The prophet, understanding this, does not ask who these women are, for that was plain to the prophetic spirit, nor what they carry, about which he had been instructed above, but where they carry it. In short, there follows: I said to the angel who spoke in me: Where are these carrying the jar? He answered: That a house may be built for it in the land of Shinar. For which the Seventy translated, in the land of Babylon. For Shinar is a plain of the Chaldeans, in which those who had moved their feet from the east, and could not stand in the service of God, built the tower of pride; whence the city itself also was called Babylon, that is, confusion, because there the tongues of all were confounded and mingled. Impiety, therefore, is carried by these women into Babylon, so that there its house may be built, and it may be established, and set upon its base, and rest in an everlasting abode. For truly in Babylon is the seat of impiety, both according to the history and according to the mystical senses.

6:1.t: And I turned, and lifted up my eyes and saw. And behold, four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains, mountains of bronze. In the first chariot were red horses, and in the second chariot black horses, and in the third chariot white horses, and in the fourth chariot spotted and strong horses. And I answered, and said to the angel who spoke in me: What are these, my lord? And the angel answered, and said to me: These are the four winds of heaven, which go out to stand before the Ruler of all the earth. The one in which were the black horses went out into the land of the north, and the white went out after them, and the spotted went out toward the land of the south. But those which were the most robust went out, and sought to go and run to and fro through all the earth. And he said: Go, walk through the earth; and they walked through the earth. And he called me, and spoke to me, saying: Behold, those who go out into the land of the north have made my spirit rest in the land of the north. […]

According to allegory, let us take in the present place too whatever we said about the four horns and the four smiths. I have read in a certain person's volume that the four chariots, in which are red, and black, and white, and spotted and strong horses, are to be understood as the four Gospels, and the horses as the apostles, possessing different graces through the diversity of the colors: of whom some are red with martyrdom, others dark and black, knowing the mysteries of Christ, of whom it is said in the psalm: Darkness was under his feet, and: He made darkness his hiding place. Others white, with the grace of virginity; others spotted and strong, having the grace of healings and of various powers.

These four kingdoms which overthrew Judea Zechariah writes that he saw in four horns, the angel saying to him: These are the horns which have scattered Judah and Israel and Jerusalem. And again: I lifted up, he says, my eyes and saw; and behold, four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze; in the first chariot, red horses; and in the second chariot, black horses; and in the third chariot, white horses; and in the fourth chariot, dappled, strong horses. And when the prophet had said to the angel who spoke in him: What are these, my lord? The angel answered: These are the four winds of heaven, which go forth to stand before the ruler of all the earth; and the sense is: These are they who go forth from the face of the Lord, to fulfill his will.

6:2.t: In the first chariot were red horses, bloody and bloodthirsty, and terrible with the cruelty of Babylon. In the second chariot, black horses, the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, which, seated in a two-horse chariot and going out through the edict of King Ahasuerus, bore before it, with sad tidings, the death of all the Jews. In the third chariot, white horses, the Macedonians, under whose king Antiochus we read of the victory of the Maccabees. In the fourth chariot, spotted, strong horses. For we know that of the kings of the Romans some were merciful toward the Jewish nation, such as Gaius Caesar, Augustus and Claudius; others persecutors and terrible, such as Gaius Caligula, Nero, Vespasian and Hadrian. For strong, which Aquila translated κρατεροὺς (strong), the Seventy ψαροὺς (dappled), in the Hebrew is written amasim. And certain copies wrongly have πυῤῥοὺς, confusing the differences of the colors and of the kingdoms, since πυῤῥοὶ, that is, red, are called not amasim but adamim.

6:4.t: So when the prophet asks what the things he saw meant to signify, the angel who spoke in him answers, and relates that they are the four winds of heaven, that is, the four quarters of the world, which the Greeks call κλίματα, which stand by and obey the will of the Lord. For these four kingdoms of which we have spoken did nothing apart from the will of the Lord.

6:5.t: These chariots, four in number, or cars, were sent into the four winds of heaven, that is, to the hinges of the world, and the whole circle of the lands, to fulfil the will of the Lord; to whom it is afterward said by the angel: Go, and walk through the earth, and sow the Gospel in all the ends of the earth.

6:6.t: The one in which were the black horses, he says, went out into the land of the north. How finely the first chariot, in which were the red horses, is passed over, and what the second and the third and the fourth did is described! For already at the time when the prophet was relating these things, the kingdom of Babylon had passed away, and the power of the Medes held all Asia; under their king Darius, in his second year, in the eleventh month, which is called Shebat, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, he beholds all that we have expounded above. The one, then, in which were the black horses went out into the land of the north, so that the might of the Medes might overthrow the kingdom of the Chaldeans. And this is to be noted, that the κλίματα, that is, the quarters of the globe and of the world, are named in the holy Scriptures according to the situation of Jerusalem and of the temple. […]

6:8.t: And turning to the prophet he testifies with a clear voice: Behold, those who go out into the land of the north have made my spirit rest in the land to which they set out. In a passage that is indeed most difficult, it was handed down to me by the Hebrews that Alexander and all the Macedonians, that is, the white horses which went out after the Medes and Persians, who had themselves also gone into the land of the north, made the prophetic spirit rest in the land of the north, because against the Medes they fulfilled the will of God, and in a short time the empire of the Medes and Persians was destroyed by the Macedonians. For great is the consolation of those who are oppressed, if they know that their enemies will soon perish. These things, as we were able, or rather as we received them, we have handed on to those devoted to our language, following the truth of the history; not hunting out with tenacious memory, after the fashion of the Egyptian exposition, the chariots of Pharaoh and the Babylonian cars; […]

This too, which follows: Behold, those who go out into the land of the north have made my spirit rest in the land of the north, he explained in such a way as to say that the spirit of the Lord, or of the angel, rested when, in the land of the north, the most harsh kingdoms of the devil were overthrown by the apostolic preaching; and that these are the kingdoms which the devil, showing them to the Lord and Savior on a high mountain, boasted had been handed over to himself.

6:10.t: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Take from the exiles, from Heldai and from Tobijah, and from Jedaiah, and you shall come on that day, and enter the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who came from Babylon. And you shall take silver and gold, and make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and you shall speak to him, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts, saying: Behold a man, the Rising is his name, and beneath him it shall rise, and he shall build a temple to the Lord. And he himself shall raise a temple to the Lord, and he himself shall bear glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne, and he shall be a priest upon his throne, and the counsel of peace shall be between the two of them. And the crowns shall be for Helem and for Tobijah and for Jedaiah and for Hen son of Zephaniah, a memorial in the temple of the Lord. And those who are far off shall come and build in the temple of the Lord, and you shall know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you. […]

But upon us lies the necessity of saying, according to the LXX translators, what our forefathers said. Take from the captivity, and from the rulers, and from its useful men, and from those who have known it, gold and silver, and having gone into the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who himself too came from Babylon, make in it crowns of gold and of silver, which you shall place upon the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. The captivity of the Jews, that is, of the people that confesses the Lord, is vices and sins, which he who has begun to do repentance and to long for the former Jerusalem, that is, the Church of Christ, abandons and leaves behind in Babylon; and it is offered by the rulers of the captives, and by its useful men, that is, of the captivity, who themselves too were handed over for their own profit to an angel of Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit might be saved; […]

6:11.t: And the crowns, or the crown, are set upon Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, because, as we advance and return to better things, the Lord is crowned through each of our virtues; or rather, as we are crowned through the virtues of repentance, the Savior receives a crown in each one, according to what Paul also says: For the rest, there is laid up for me a crown of justice, which the Lord, the just judge, will render to me; and not to me only, but also to all who love the coming of our Lord Savior Jesus Christ. Whence the father of the Lord Savior also took his name from the crown of justice. For Jehozadak is interpreted Lord of justice, because he renders to each according to his works. Of this crown James too speaks in his epistle: Blessed is the man who endures temptation, for when he has been proved he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him.

And when you have made the crowns, you shall set one of them on the head of Joshua (Iesus, the same name as Jesus) son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and you shall speak to him: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold a man whose name is the Rising, which in Hebrew is called sema, written not with the letter sin but with sade. He is called the Rising, that is, ἀνατολὴ, or ἀναφύη, or βλάστημα, that is, shoot, for this reason: because he shall suddenly spring up of himself, and shall sprout from his own root in the likeness of a shoot; and this man shall build the temple of the Lord.

6:12.t:
But in all battles He triumphed over the devil, and all the unseen enemies and foes led by him, and made us who were slaves His own people, and built of us, as of living stones, the house of God, and the state of holiness, so that He exactly agrees with the oracle, which says:

"Behold a man, whose name is the Branch. And he shall spring up from below, and shall build the house of the Lord. And he shall receive virtue, and shall sit and rule upon his throne."

Note, therefore, with care, in what manner in speaking mystically of the Jesus of days of old, who bears the image of the true, he says: "Behold a man, whose name is the Branch." And a little later, it is said to Jesus himself then present, as if concerning some one else who was the Branch: "Hear, Jesus, the High Priest, thou and thy neighbour, for the men are diviners. Behold, I bring my servant the Branch." […]
6:12.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 4, Chapter 17

6:12.t: And the prophet is commanded, after he has placed the crown, or the crowns, upon the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, to speak to him and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold a man, the Rising is his name, and beneath him it shall rise, and the rest. We do not divide Jesus, nor can we make two persons in one person, but he who is called Jesus because he saved the world is himself also called the Rising, because in his days justice has risen. And it is sung in the psalm: Truth has risen from the earth, because, begotten from a virgin's womb at the consummation of the ages, he said: I am the truth, and he came at the last hour, according to the epistle of John, who says: Little children, it is now the last hour, in which he hired for a denarius the people of the nations, who were standing and doing nothing, and sent them to the vineyard. […]

And beneath him shall rise the multitude of believers, and he shall build the house of the Lord, the Church, and he himself shall receive the power and beauty and progress and glory of each one, and shall sit and rule on his throne, on the throne of David, of which it is also written in the Gospel: And there shall be a priest at his right hand, or, according to the Hebrew, upon his throne, because he himself is both king and high priest, and shall sit on the royal as well as on the priestly throne, and there shall be a peaceful counsel between the two, so that neither shall the royal eminence depress the priestly dignity, nor the dignity of the priesthood the royal eminence, but both shall agree in the glory of the one Lord Jesus. I have read in a certain person's book that what is said: And a peaceful counsel shall be between the two, refers to the Father and to the Son, because he came to do not his own will but the Father's, and the Father is in the Son, and the Son in the Father.

6:13.t: And when he has raised it, he himself also shall bear glory, that is, the second crown, which in Hebrew is hod, and is written by one ἐπιδοξότης, by another εὐπρέπεια, by another ἀρετὴ, by another δόξα; which mean either renown, or beauty, or virtue, or glory. And they think Zerubbabel is signified, who, rising suddenly from a lowly man and a captive to be leader of the Jewish people, built the temple of the Lord, and sat upon his throne, and ruled with the power of a prince; but the high priest too, he says, Joshua son of Jehozadak, shall sit on the priestly throne, and with minds and counsels joined they shall govern the people of God.

And there shall be peace between those two, that is, between him who is of the royal tribe and him who descends from the Levitical stock, so that priesthood and kingdom alike may rule the people of God; and the crowns themselves which you have made of gold and silver, after they have been set on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak and on the head of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, you shall consecrate in the temple with the names of those by whom they were offered, that is, of Helem, and Tobijah, and Jedaiah, and Hen. The second and third names are the same as above. The first has been changed; for in place of Heldai he has now put Helem; a fourth, which he had not mentioned above, has been added, that is, Hen; of these we shall speak in what follows.

6:14.t: Heldai is interpreted the entreaty of the Lord, which in Greek is said more expressively λιτάνευσις κυρίου. Tobijah, good of the Lord. Jedaiah, known of the Lord. In place of Heldai he has now put in the first place Helem, which means dream; and in the fourth place he has added Hen, that is, grace. The crowns of these four men shall be with the son of Zephaniah, whom we read above was Josiah, who is the guardian and warden of the temple of the Lord, and there they shall rest in an everlasting abode. The Hebrews relate that Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael, coming from the captivity, brought gold and silver as gifts for the temple, and the crowns of the high priest and of the leader; and that Hen, whom he had not mentioned above, that is, grace, means Daniel, who came with a gift; and that Helem was put in place of Heldai for this reason, so that from the interpretation of the name, which means dream, it might be shown that Daniel, set in captivity, and the three young men knew the mysteries of the king's dream. […]

And the crown, that is, the emblem of victory, once Christ has been crowned, is promised also to those who wait for him, and understand the profit of their former captivity, and know all the mysteries of God, so that they may be for the favor of the son of Zephaniah, that is, of the visitation of the Lord.

And those who said in Babylon: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept, when we remembered Zion; on the willows in the midst of it we hung up our instruments, once they have returned to Jerusalem, let them take up psalm and timbrel, and sing in the Church of the Lord; and let those who through greater sins had been far from Judea come, with a most true confession too, and through each of their advances build the house of the Lord; and then let all with one mind know that the Lord Almighty has sent the prophet to them. And all that has been promised shall come to pass, if they are willing to hear the Lord, and, having done repentance, remain in good works.

6:15.t: And when the crowns, he says, have been laid up in the temple of the Lord, and consecrated for an everlasting memorial, nations from the whole circle of the lands and set far off shall come, and shall build in my temple, each according to his strength. And then, by the outcome of events and the prosperity of all, you shall know that the Lord has sent me, and that at his command I foretold all things. And all these things shall come to pass if you obey the precepts of the Lord and do his commandments.

7:1.t: And it came to pass in the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, on the fourth of the ninth month, which is Chislev. And Sharezer and Regem-melech, and the men who were with him, sent to the house of God, to entreat the face of the Lord, to speak to the priests of the house of the Lord of hosts and to the prophets, saying: Must I weep in the fifth month, or ought I to sanctify myself, as I have done now for many years? And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying: Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and the seventh through these seventy years, did you fast a fast to me? And when you ate and drank? Did you not eat for yourselves and drink for your own selves? Are these not the words which the Lord spoke by the hand of the former prophets, when Jerusalem was still inhabited and was wealthy, she and her cities round about her, and it was inhabited toward the south and in the plains? […]

7:2.t: What is written in the Seventy, Sharezer and Arabesser the king sent from Bethel, none of our writers has been able to expound; for what has been badly translated from the Hebrew cannot be explained by any reasoning. For who is this Sharezer, or Arabesser the king? Or king of what province? Or into which Bethel, or from which, did he send? Or of what Bethel could Arabesser be king, a place that had long before been left desolate together with Judea, and at that time was by no means called Bethel, that is, house of God, but Beth-aven, that is, house of an idol?

7:3.t: This too which follows, Sanctification has come in here in the fifth month, as they had done now through many years, they try to expound thus: that the sanctification which came in is the vessels of the temple, which had been carried off by Nebuchadnezzar, restored at that time. As for the fast of the fifth and the seventh, they tried to refer it to the days of the week. But since the fast of the tenth follows, they were compelled to refer it to months, and as to what this fast of the fifth, seventh and tenth month itself is, they were entirely silent. Hence let us be content with the former explanation, and let us not incline to the false attempts of the commentators, which came from an error of translation.

7:4.t: After the generals of the Persians had made their inquiry through those whom they had sent, and the embassy of the inquirers to the priests and prophets had been carried out, the word of the Lord came to the prophet, commanding him to speak to the common people and to the priests, telling them what they ought to answer the envoys. When you fasted and mourned in the fifth month, that of the captivity of Jerusalem, and in the seventh month, when Gedaliah was slain by Ishmael, through the seventy years of the desolation of the temple and of the overthrow of Jerusalem, was it of any profit to me that you fasted? And on the other hand, whenever you eat and drink, is it not for yourselves that you both eat and drink? For God is not appeased by these things, but by good works, and if we do his commandments, because food does not commend us to God. Neither, if we do not eat, shall we lack; nor, if we eat, shall we abound.

7:7.t: Are not these my words, while Jerusalem and the cities of Judah were still standing, which I spoke to you by the hands of my prophets, when Jerusalem still stood, and the cities of Judah abounded in all things, and both the hill country and the plain overflowed with crops and enjoyed a most secure peace? Now these were the words of the Lord, as the Scripture that follows testifies: that he wills true judgment and mercy toward one's neighbors, and that one not wrong the widow and the orphan and the stranger and the poor, and not devise evil in one's heart. These things, he says, they would not do, and with deaf ears they despised my commands; for which reason great indignation came upon Jerusalem; and as they would not hear me, so I too did not hear them; and now they ask with such scrupulousness when they ought to fast and mourn, although I said before through Isaiah: This is not the fast I have chosen, says the Lord, nor that a man should humble his soul; […]

7:9.t: And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts, saying: Judge true judgment, and show mercy and compassion, every man with his brother. And do not wrong the widow and the orphan and the stranger and the poor; and let no man devise evil against his brother in his heart. And they would not attend, and they turned a withdrawing shoulder; and they made their ears heavy, that they might not hear; and they made their heart adamant lest they hear the law and the words which the Lord of hosts sent in his spirit by the hand of the former prophets, and great indignation came from the Lord of hosts. And it came to pass as he spoke, and they did not hear: so they shall cry, and I will not hear, says the Lord of hosts. And I scattered them through all the kingdoms which they do not know; and the land was left desolate by them, because there was none passing through and returning; and they made the desirable land into a desert. […]

7:10.t: And Zechariah also, among the twelve prophets, pointing out to the people the will of God, says: "These things does the Lord Omnipotent declare: Execute true judgment, and show mercy and compassion each one to his brother. And oppress not the widow, and the orphan, and the proselyte, and the poor; and let none imagine evil against your brother in his heart." And again, he says: "These are the words which ye shall utter. Speak ye the truth every man to his neighbour, and execute peaceful judgment in your gates, and let none of you imagine evil in his heart against his brother, and ye shall not love false swearing: for all these things I hate, saith the Lord Almighty." Moreover, David also says in like manner: "What man is there who desireth life, and would fain see good days? Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips that they speak no guile. Shun evil, and do good: seek peace, and pursue it." […]

And therefore this question must at once be determined, whether the discipline of patience is enjoined by the Creator? When by Zechariah he commanded, "Let none of you imagine evil against his brother," he did not expressly include his "neighbor;" but then in another passage he says, "Let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbor." He who counseled that an injury should be forgotten was still more likely to counsel the patient endurance of it.

The widow too, and the orphan, concerning whom we have been commanded: Be a father to orphans, and in place of a husband to their mother; judging the orphan and justifying the widow. And do not wrong the stranger and the poor, because sojourning abroad makes the one lowly, and need the other. And let no man devise evil against his brother in his heart, or, as it is said by the Seventy: And let each one not remember the malice of his brother in their hearts. By brother and neighbor we ought to understand either the whole race of men, because we are begotten of one parent, or those who are of the household of the faith, according to the parable of the Gospel, which wants the neighbor to be understood not as a blood relative but as all men. […]

7:11.t: Though I had commanded these things, they would not attend, and turned a withdrawing shoulder, or a scornful back, rejecting my commands by the bearing of their body. For when, with wrinkled brow and contracted nostril, we scorn those who admonish us, we are accustomed to turn our back; according to what is written: They turned their backs to me, and not their faces. And they made their ears heavy, he says, lest they hear, like the ears of the deaf asp that stops its ears, which will not hear the voice of the charmers, and of the sorcerer who charms wisely. For they made their ears heavy so as not to hear, and they set their heart so as not to yield to the law of God. Hence Isaiah speaks to them threateningly: The heart of this people has grown fat, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and they have closed their eyes, lest perhaps they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.

We can also refer these things to those who, sinning in the Church, have been cast out of the land of confession, because they would not hear the Lord, and turned a withdrawing shoulder to him, and made their ears heavy, and made their heart adamant. And the indignation of the Lord came upon them, and they were scattered through all the kingdoms of the vices, and their land was made desolate, whether soul or body, not having God as its inhabitant, nor the spirit returning into it. And the land once desirable, which was the lodging of the Trinity, was turned into a desert and a dwelling of dragons. Let us pass quickly over what is plain, so that there may be room for discussion in what is obscure; for we are not writing long and florid treatises, in which a speech that seeks applause plays, but commentaries, whose office is to pass over what is evident and to discuss what is obscure.

7:12.t: Moreover, what is said according to the Hebrew, And they made their heart adamant, shows hardness of heart, and a heart of stone, in that they would not receive the words of God. For adamant, a very strong stone, which in Hebrew is called samir, is so hard that it breaks all metals and is itself broken by none. Hence it is called untamable by the Greeks. With this adamant the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, so that he would not let the people of God go.

And because they had, nay rather made, their heart adamant, esteeming hardness of heart by their own will, so as not to hear the words of the Lord which he sent in his spirit, that is, in the Holy Spirit, by the hand of the former prophets, Isaiah, Hosea and the rest, who had clean hands, and who, it is plain, were before the captivity: therefore, for great sins, great indignation came about, and the words of the Lord were fulfilled, who repays like for like, so that, as they walked perversely toward him, he too should go perversely against them, and not hear the words of those crying out, because they too had despised the words of the Lord with a deaf ear.

7:13.t:
Since this is the case and since we keep none of the Lord's commands, why do we complain of God, who has far more right to complain of us? Why should we grieve that he does not hear us, when we ourselves do not hear him? What right have we to whisper that God does not look upon the earth, when we ourselves do not look up to the heavens? What reason have we to be vexed that our prayers are despised by the Lord, whose commands we despise?

Suppose that we were equal to our Lord; what chance is there for just complaint when each side receives the same treatment it gives? And this entirely overlooks a point easily proved, that we are very far from receiving what we give, since God really treats us much more kindly than we do him. For the moment, however, let us act on the assumption that I proposed. The Lord himself spoke thus: "I cried unto you and ye did not hear me: you too shall cry unto me and I shall not hear you." What is more fair and just than this? We have not hearkened, therefore he does not hear us. […]
7:13.s: On the Government of God, Book 3, Chapter 9

7:14.t: For which reason he also scattered them through all the kingdoms which they do not know, those of the Assyrians and Chaldeans, of the Medes and Persians, and of the other nations which lay subject to these empires and in whose lands they were sown abroad. And all Judea was deserted, because it had no inhabitant, and there was none in it passing through and returning. And the land which was a honeycomb above all lands, and for the greatness of its abundance flowed with milk and honey, they turned into a wilderness.

8:2.t: And the word of the Lord of hosts came, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: I have been jealous for Zion with a great jealousy, and with great indignation I have been jealous for her. Thus says the Lord of hosts: I have returned to Zion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem shall be called the city of truth, and the mountain of the Lord of hosts, the sanctified mountain. LXX: And the word of the Lord Almighty came, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with a great jealousy, and with very great fury I have been jealous for her. Thus says the Lord Almighty: I will return to Zion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem shall be called the true city, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty, the holy mountain. That the Lord took Jerusalem, that is, the Israelite people, in the wilderness as a wife, and, as she lay in the blood of idolatry, covered her with his cloak and cherished her with a husband's love, we learn more fully in Ezekiel; […]

8:4.t: But if we refer it to the Church, of which it is said: Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God, and: The rush of the river gladdens the city of God; the Most High has sanctified his tabernacle; God in the midst of her shall not be moved, who can doubt that the streets of the Church are the virtues, in which wisdom acts confidently and is proclaimed on the tops of the walls? Hence the psalmist too cries out to the Lord: Your commandment is exceedingly broad. Seeking the Lord and Savior in these streets, the bride says in the Song of Songs: I will rise and go about the city, in the market and in its streets, until I find him whom my soul has loved. So there shall dwell, or sit, old men and old women, of whom it is written — if, however, anyone is pleased to receive the book —: Honorable old age is not that of long time, nor is it reckoned by the number of years. But grey hairs are men's prudence, and a spotless life is old age; […]

Thus says the Lord of hosts. Old men and old women shall yet dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and a man's staff in his hand for the multitude of days. And the streets of the city shall be filled with infants and girls, playing in its streets. LXX: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Old men and old women shall yet sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each one holding his rod in his hand, for the multitude of days; and the streets of the city shall be filled with boys and girls, playing in its streets. So great, he says, once I have returned to Zion and am dwelling in the midst of Jerusalem, will be the prosperity of all things and the rest and tranquillity from wars, that, with no enemy remaining, old age in both sexes will reach the furthest span of life and support its trembling limbs with a guiding staff. The streets of the city too shall be filled with boys and girls playing. […]

8:5.t: This is that wine with which, when youths and maidens are intoxicated, they at once thirst for virginity. They are filled with the spirit of chastity, and the prophecy of Zechariah comes to pass, at least if we follow the Hebrew literally, for he prophesied concerning virgins: "And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof. For what is his goodness, and what is his beauty, but the corn of the elect, and wine that gives birth to virgins?" They are virgins of whom it is written in the forty-fifth psalm: "She is led to the king, with her virgin companions, her escort, in her train. With joy and gladness they are led along as they enter the palace of the king."

Old men and old women of this sort shall sit in the streets of Jerusalem, and shall hold staffs in their hands, and the streets of the city shall be filled with boys and girls playing. These are the boys and girls, the old men and the young, whom the psalmist exhorts to sing to the Lord, saying: Young men and maidens, old men with the younger, let them praise the name of the Lord. And John, the evangelist and apostle: I write, he says, to you, children, because your sins are forgiven you for the name of the Savior. I write to you, fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning. And of these Solomon speaks in Proverbs: To give shrewdness to the innocent; and to the younger boy sense and understanding. And again: Hear, children, the instruction of a father, and attend, that you may know understanding. […]

8:6.t: Thus says the Lord of hosts: If it shall seem difficult in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, shall it be difficult in my eyes? says the Lord of hosts. LXX: Thus says the Lord Almighty: If it shall be impossible before the remnant of this people in those days, shall it also be impossible before me? says the Lord Almighty. At each of the words and sentences in which prosperity is promised to Israel, and which, because of the greatness of the things, seem almost incredible, the prophet sets forth: Thus says the Lord Almighty; saying this in other words: Do not think that the things I pledge are mine, and do not disbelieve them as though they came from a man; the promises I unfold are God's. He had said above that old women and old men would sit in the streets and, for the length of their time, would hold staffs in their hands; that the streets would be thronged with a multitude of people; that boys and girls would lead dances as on feast days; […]

8:7.t: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting of the sun. And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in justice. LXX: likewise. Some of the Jews say that these things were fulfilled after Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, when the temple had been built, the walls of the city raised and the Jewish state restored, by the Maccabees and the various princes who ruled Judea down to Herod. Others relate that they are to be fulfilled at the consummation of the world under the Christ, for whom they wait in vain. But we say that they were both partly fulfilled at that time, that is, after Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, and went before as it were in types and images, when the people was brought back from captivity and dwelt in Jerusalem and was called the people of God, and the Lord was again called their God, by no means in falsehood and iniquity but in truth and justice; […]

8:8.t: And what follows, In truth and justice, signifies that the shadow of the old law departs and the truth of the Gospel comes, by no means in the justice of the Jews, but in Christian justice; for the Lord himself is truth and justice, of whom we read: Truth has risen from the earth, and justice has looked down from heaven. Hence in Psalm 14 (15) too justice and truth are named together: He who walks without blemish and works justice, and speaks truth in his heart.

8:9.t: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Let your hands be strengthened, you who hear in these days these words through the mouth of the prophets, on the day on which the house of the Lord of hosts was founded, that the temple might be built. The Seventy translated "the Lord Almighty" for "the Lord of hosts", the rest likewise. The temple having been built under Zerubbabel and Joshua (for it was in the fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is called Chislev), all these things are said when the temple had already been raised; the same prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, who had exhorted both the leaders and the people that it might be built, now exhort them, so that from the truth of the earlier things they may lend faith to those which are promised for the future; and that they may strengthen their hands, in no way fearing the onset of the Medes and the plots of the surrounding nations who desire to hinder them; […]

8:10.t: For before those days there was no wage for men, nor was there a wage for beasts, nor was there peace for him who came in and went out, because of the tribulation; and I let loose all men, each one against his neighbor. LXX: For before those days the wage of men shall not be for gain, and the wage of beasts shall not stand, and for him who goes out and him who comes in there shall be no peace because of the tribulation; and I will send forth all men, each one to his neighbor. The Seventy referred everything to future time, but it is better referred to the past, as it stands in the Hebrew, and the truth of the exposition will bear this out. Before the house of the Lord was founded and the temple of the Lord was built, all your labor was in vain. And men as well as beasts, in farming, in trading and in various works, were frustrated in empty efforts; […]

8:11.t: But now I will not deal with the remnant of this people as in the former days, says the Lord of hosts, but there shall be a seed of peace. The vine shall give its fruit and the earth shall give its shoot; and the heavens shall give their dew, and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things. LXX: And now I will not deal with the remnant of this people as in the former days, says the Lord Almighty, but I will show peace. The vine shall give its fruit and the earth shall give its shoots; and heaven shall give its dew, and I will cause the remnant of my people to possess all these things. Before the foundations of the house of God were laid and the temple was built, there was no wage for men, nor a wage for beasts, nor, because of tribulation and distress, peace for those who came in and went out, and all men were at variance among themselves with hostile hatred. […]

8:12.t: The vine shall give its fruit, the vine that says in the Gospel: I am the vine, you are the branches. Every branch that abides in me, the Father cleanses, that it may bear greater fruit. And when its branches have been cleansed, that is, its shoots and layers, and with budding eyes have begun to promise the hope of fruits to come, so that what is written may be fulfilled: The flowering vines have given forth their fragrance, then the sun of justice has colored the hanging clusters, so that, sent into the winepresses of Psalms 8 and 83 (84), which are entitled for the winepresses, they may be trodden by the foot of the Lord, who comes up from Bozrah, that he may pour out the wine that gladdens the heart of man. The earth too shall give its shoot, not the dry and stony earth full of thorns, but the good earth which yields fruit a hundredfold and sixtyfold and thirtyfold, so that those who have sown in tears may reap in joy. […]

8:13.t: And it shall be: as you were a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you and you shall be a blessing: do not fear, let your hands be strengthened. For thus says the Lord of hosts: As I purposed to afflict you, when your fathers had provoked me to anger, says the Lord, and I did not have mercy, so, having turned, I have purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: do not fear. LXX: And it shall be: as you were in a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you shall be in a blessing; take courage and be strengthened in your hearts, for thus says the Lord Almighty. As I purposed to afflict you in that your fathers had provoked me to anger, says the Lord Almighty, and I did not repent, so I am ready and have purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: take courage. […]

But concerning the Church and each one of the believers it can be understood thus: that in the time of persecution the Christians were a curse and an example to all the nations round about, because they had offended their Lord; and afterwards they are in blessing, when peace has been restored; and all this comes about because the Lord, who had at first been angry, afterwards has mercy on Jerusalem, the vision of peace, and on Judah, which confesses the faith of the Lord. Each of the believers, too, who are cast out of the Church for their vices and are handed over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that they may learn not to blaspheme, when they have done repentance, will return to their former state and will see the peace of the Lord, and will possess the glory of their confession.

8:14.t: What is written, I did not have mercy, or I did not repent, the heretics slander, as though the Lord were either cruel or changeable, if he either does not repent or repents. For if he has repented, they say that he is changeable; if he has not repented, they assert that he is cruel. Yet God repented that he had anointed Saul as king. And among the Ninevites, to whom he had announced through the prophet: Yet three days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown, because they did repentance, he himself too is said to have changed his sentence, not through the fault of an improvident mind, but from the difference in what they do, badly or well. For if they do evil, he threatens; if they have blotted out their former sins, he has mercy; God is not changed, who is one and the same and cannot be changed, but when they have changed from evil to good works, he himself also changes his own decree. He it is who also speaks in Genesis: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has been multiplied, and their sins are exceedingly great; […]

The cause of the strengthening is the Lord's promise: For thus says the Lord Almighty, to whom nothing is impossible, who is able to fulfil what he promises: As I devised to afflict you and to hand you over to captivity, because your fathers provoked me to anger, and I did not have mercy, which the LXX translated οὐ μετενόησα, that is, I did not repent, which in Hebrew is written ulo naamathi; but I did not have mercy, so that I might correct you by captivity and train you through every torment and scourge; so now, in the present time, I have purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. And it is to be noted that when he is angry, the house of Judah and the house of Israel, that is, all twelve tribes which were handed over to captivity, are a curse among the nations. But after he has purposed to do good, he does not do it to Judah and Israel, that is, to the two and the ten tribes, namely to Jerusalem and Samaria, Oholah and Oholibah; […]

8:16.t: For indeed there is nothing equal to this virtue. Wouldest thou learn the power of this virtue? "Though Moses and Samuel stood before Me," saith God, "my soul would not regard them." Nevertheless, those whom Moses and Samuel were not able to snatch away from God's wrath, this precept when observed was able to snatch away. Hence it is, that He continually exhorts those to whom He had spoken these things, saying, "Let none of you revengefully imagine evil against his brother in your heart," and "let none of you think of his neighbour's malice." It is not said merely, forego wrath; but retain it not in thy mind; think not of it; part with all thy resentment; do away the sore. For thou supposest that thou art paying him back the injury; but thou art first tormenting thyself, and setting up thy rage as an executioner within thee in every part, and tearing up thine own bowels. For what can be more wretched than a man perpetually angry? […]

These, then, are the words which you shall do: Speak the truth, each one with his neighbor; judge truth and the judgment of peace in your gates; and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his friend, and do not love a lying oath; for all these are things that I hate, says the Lord. LXX: These are the words which you shall do: Speak the truth, each one with his neighbor, and a peaceable judgment, judge in your gates, and let each one not devise evil against his neighbor in your hearts, and do not love a lying oath, for all these things I hate, says the Lord Almighty. I have promised that I will not deal with the remnant of the people of the captives as in the former days. And as I purposed to afflict them, when their fathers had provoked me to anger, and I did not have mercy, so now, having turned, I have purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. […]

8:17.t: And do not devise evil, he says, against your friends in your hearts; raath, which all with one voice have translated κακίαν, that is, evil, we can take in two ways, both for affliction and for wickedness. For affliction: If there is evil in a city which the Lord has not done, and: Sufficient for the day is its own evil. For wickedness, God speaks in the prophet Jonah: The cry of their evil has gone up to me, and in the Apostle we read: Filled with all iniquity and evil. In both ways, therefore, he who is holy neither afflicts his friend nor devises evil against him in his heart. And do not love, he says, a lying oath; for the Lord commands in the Gospel: But I say to you, do not swear at all, but let your speech be, yes yes, no no; for he who does not swear will never be able to swear falsely. Let him who swears hear what is written: You shall not take up the name of the Lord your God in a vain thing. […]

8:19.t: Therefore let us also, when we come to the feast, no longer come as to old shadows, for they are accomplished, neither as to common feasts, but let us hasten as to the Lord, Who is Himself the feast, not looking upon it as an indulgence and delight of the belly, but as a manifestation of virtue. For the feasts of the heathen are full of greediness, and utter indolence, since they consider they celebrate a feast when they are idle; and they work the works of perdition when they feast. But our feasts consist in the exercise of virtue and the practice of temperance; as the prophetic word testifies in a certain place, saying, ‘The fast of the fourth, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth [month], shall be to the house of Judah for gladness, and rejoicing, and for pleasant feasts.’ […]

And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: The fast of the fourth, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth shall be to the house of Judah for joy and for gladness, and for glorious solemn feasts; only love truth and peace. LXX: And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty: The fourth fast, and the fifth fast, and the seventh fast, and the tenth fast shall be to the house of Judah for joy and for gladness, and for good festivals; — for in Hebrew this is said tobim, that is, ἀγαθάς —, and rejoice, and love truth and peace. […]

8:20.t: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Until peoples come, and dwell in many cities, and the inhabitants go one to another, saying: Let us go and entreat the face of the Lord, and let us seek the Lord of hosts. I too will go, and many peoples and strong nations shall come to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to entreat the face of the Lord. LXX: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Many peoples shall yet come, and the inhabitants of many cities; and those who dwell in the cities shall be gathered into one city, saying: Let us go to entreat the face of the Lord, and let us seek the countenance of the Lord Almighty. I too will go, and many peoples and very many nations shall come, to seek the face of the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem, and to entreat the face of the Lord. The fast of the fourth, and of the fifth, and of the seventh, and of the tenth month shall be changed into excellent solemn feasts, so much so that the cities of Judea which before were deserted shall be thronged with many inhabitants; […]

8:23.t: Thus says the Lord of hosts: In those days, in which ten men of all the tongues of the nations shall take hold, and they shall take hold of the hem of a man who is a Jew, saying: We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you. LXX: Thus says the Lord Almighty: In those days, if ten men of all the tongues of the nations take hold, and grasp the hem of a man who is a Jew, saying: We will go with you, because we have heard that God is with you. Some of the Jews say that these things were fulfilled under Zerubbabel and after Zerubbabel. Others put them off to a future time, when they hope that the Christ will come. But we understand them both more rightly and more truly of the coming of the Lord and Savior, when he was born of the virgin Mary. In short, it is written: Until peoples come? […]

9:1.t: The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and of Damascus his rest, for the eye of man is the Lord's, and of all the tribes of Israel. LXX: The taking up of the word of the Lord in the land of Sedrach and of Damascus his sacrifice, for the Lord looks upon men, and all the tribes of Israel. This whole vision, or weight and burden of the word of the Lord, as Aquila translated it, pertains to the calling of the nations and the building of the Church. And the order of the words is: The taking up of the word of the Lord, sharp toward sinners, soft toward the just. For Hadrach, a name compounded of two whole words, sounds this: ad meaning sharp, rach soft and tender, and not, as it is wrongly read by some, Sedrach. Some refer Hadrach to the people of the Jews, Damascus to the calling of the nations. […]

9:2.t: Hamath also on its borders, and Tyre and Sidon, for they have taken to themselves exceeding wisdom. And Tyre built her fortification, and heaped up silver like dust, and gold like the mud of the streets. Behold, the Lord shall possess her, and shall strike her strength in the sea, and she shall be devoured by fire. LXX: And Hamath on its borders, Tyre and Sidon, since they were exceedingly wise, and Tyre built her fortification, and gathered silver like dust, and gold like the mud of the roads. Therefore the Lord shall possess her, and shall strike her strength in the sea, and she shall be burned up in fire. Hamath, which is interpreted χόλος, that is, wrath, is the same city that received the name Epiphania from Antiochus Ἐπιφανεῖ (Epiphanes), and is now a city of Coele Syria. […]

But Tyre and Sidon — of which the one is interpreted συνοχὴ, that is, distress, the other θήρευμα, that is, hunting —, took to themselves wisdom to such a degree that, with its sophisms and the nets of dialectic and the webs of the sophists, which Scripture calls fortifications, Tyre put riddles to Solomon, that is, to the peaceful king; and gathered its silver, namely the brilliance of eloquence, and its gold, the cunning of its thoughts, like the dust and mud that lie in the streets and roads, so as to possess the kingdom of idolatry that it had fortified. But against these fortifications the Apostle speaks: For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty to God for the destruction of fortifications, destroying reasonings and every height that exalts itself against the knowledge of God. […]

9:4.t: And so the Lord shall possess both Tyre and Sidon, when he has first struck their strength in the most salt and most bitter sea of this world; and, lest anything of their former wisdom remain in them, that is, of the swollen folly through which they procured for themselves feeble fortifications, and silver and gold like mud, he will smelt them with fire and cleanse them to purity; of which the Savior speaks in the Gospel: I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish that it were kindled, according to what is written in Mark: Everyone shall be salted with fire.

9:5.t: Ashkelon shall see and fear, and Gaza, and shall grieve exceedingly; and Ekron, because her hope is confounded, and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited. And the separator shall sit in Ashdod, and I will destroy the pride of the Philistines. And I will take away his blood from his mouth and his abominations from between his teeth, and he too shall be left to our God, and he shall be as a leader in Judah, and Ekron as the Jebusite. And I will surround my house with those who fight as soldiers for me, going and returning, and the exactor shall no more pass over them, for now I have seen with my eyes. LXX: Ashkelon shall see and fear, and Gaza, and shall grieve exceedingly; and Ekron, because she is confounded in her hope, and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited. […]

9:6.t: And when Ashkelon, Gaza and Ekron have been terrified, and have grieved because they either had no inhabitants, or lost their king, or their former hope was frustrated, foreigners shall sit in Ashdod, where the fire generates which the Lord sent upon the earth and desires to be kindled. For he baptizes in the Holy Spirit and fire, where there is the cousin and the paternal uncle, ἀδελφὶδος καὶ πατράδελφος, whom the bride desires in the Song of Songs; where there is the fire of the breast and of the most bounteous bosom, of which we read in the same Song: He shall abide between my breasts, and in the Apostle: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food. Where according to the LXX we said: And foreigners shall dwell in Ashdod, in the Hebrew is read, the mamzer shall dwell, or shall sit, in Ashdod, for which we have put: And the separator shall sit in Ashdod. […]

9:7.t: And he shall take away from their mouth the blood, words of blasphemy, and the abominations, the worship of idols and the eating of things sacrificed to idols, from between their teeth, so that, after these have been taken away, the Philistines themselves, that is, the foreigners, may be left to the Lord, and may be a leader in Judah, that is, among the people that confesses the Lord, so that the former people which was at the head may be turned into the tail, and the last, which was at the tail, may pass to the head; and that Ekron, once barren and for that reason uprooted, may be as Jebus, that is, as Jerusalem. For this city is called by three names, Jebus, Salem and Jerusalem.

9:8.t: And I will surround, he says, my house, that is, the Church, with those who fight as soldiers for me, that is, with those who serve me in various mysteries, and at my command run hither and thither, going and coming back. Or: I will surround my house with the protection of the angels, of whom it is also written in another place: The angel of the Lord shall send round about those who fear him, and shall deliver them, so that there may be no one who goes and returns, that is, who plots ambushes against my people. Nor shall the exactor pass over it any more, of whom Isaiah says: The exactor has ceased, or else ἐξελαύνων, that is, one who leads out of doors, and drags the bound into captivity, for with his eyes, which we can understand as the prophets and all the saints, the Lord saw the calling of the nations and the security of the Church.

9:9.t: "And that expression, 'binding his foal to the vine, and the ass's foal to the vine tendril,' was a declaring beforehand both of the works wrought by Him at His first advent, and also of that belief in Him which the nations would repose. For they were like an unharnessed foal, which was not bearing a yoke on its neck, until this Christ came, and sent His disciples to instruct them; and they bore the yoke of His word, and yielded the neck to endure all [hardships], for the sake of the good things promised by Himself, and expected by them. And truly our Lord Jesus Christ, when He intended to go into Jerusalem, requested His disciples to bring Him a certain ass, along with its foal, which was bound in an entrance of a village called Bethphage; and having seated Himself on it, He entered into Jerusalem. And as this was done by Him in the manner in which it was prophesied in precise terms that it would be done by the Christ, and as the fulfilment was recognised, it became a clear proof that He was the Christ. […]

A spiritual disciple of this sort truly receiving the Spirit of God, who was from the beginning, in all the dispensations of God, present with mankind, and announced things future, revealed things present, and narrated things past-[such a man] does indeed "judge all men, but is himself judged by no man." For he judges the Gentiles, "who serve the creature more than the Creator," and with a reprobate mind spend all their labour on vanity. And he also judges the Jews, who do not accept of the word of liberty, nor are willing to go forth free, although they have a Deliverer present [with them]; but they pretend, at a time unsuitable [for such conduct], to serve, [with observances] beyond [those required by] the law, God who stands in need of nothing, and do not recognise the advent of Christ, which He accomplished for the salvation of men, nor are willing to understand that all the prophets announced His two advents: the one, indeed, in which He became a man subject to stripes, and knowing what it is to bear infirmity, […]

At another time, he speaks of us under the figure of a colt. He means by [the colt] that we are unyoked to evil, unsubdued by wickedness, unaffected, high-spirited only with him our Father. We are colts, not stallions, "who whinny lustfully for their neighbor's wife, beasts of burden unrestrained in their lust." Rather, we are free and newly born, joyous in our faith, holding fast to the course of truth, swift in seeking salvation, spurning and trampling upon worldliness. "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion. Shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, your king comes to you, the just and the Savior, and he is poor and riding upon an ass and upon a young colt." He is not satisfied to say "colt"; he adds "young" to emphasize humankind's rejuvenation in Christ and its unending, eternal youth and simplicity. Our divine Tamer trains such young colts as we little ones. Although the passage speaks of a young ass, it too is a colt.

Everywhere the cause of the unbelief of the Jews was this: that they did not understand Jesus as the "Christ of God", because they always gave their mind to the corporeal histories, unwilling to believe anything spiritual in them. For example, we introduce for the sake of illustration what is prophesied and said in Zechariah, that as it were "upon an ass and a colt He would enter into Jerusalem and would destroy the chariots out of Ephraim and the horse out of Jerusalem". If anyone wishes to understand this of Christ according to the history of the letter, it does not fit; for Christ is nowhere expounded to have destroyed out of Ephraim corporeal and perceptible chariots, nor a corporeal horse from a corporeal Jerusalem. But if you see among the heretics the assemblies of falsehood itself coupled together as by a certain yoke and in evil concord among themselves, which the word of truth is wont to destroy, you will see how Christ, the Word of God, destroys the spiritual chariots out of the spiritual Ephraim; […]

So prophesied Zechariah after the Return from Babylon, in the reign of Darius, King of Persia, when Jerusalem was but just arisen from the desolation which it suffered under the Babylonians. And the whole period from Darius the Persian, in whose time Zechariah prophesied, even to Augustus, Emperor of Rome, amounts to the seven and sixty-two weeks of years in Daniel, which are equivalent to 483 years, as I have shewn in my recent investigations. And neither in the time of the Macedonians from Alexander onwards, not even if you include the reign of Augustus, was anything similar to the words of the prophet fulfilled. For when in those days did the Lord, Whom the prophet speaks of as divine, come among men, and many nations know Him, and confess Him to the only God, and take refuge in Him, and be to Him a people? Or when in the times of the Macedonians or Persians did the king who was foretold come, sitting upon an ass and a young colt? […]
9:9.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 4

9:9.t:
[Passage quoted, Zech. ix. 9, 10]

As Zechariah prophesied thus after the Return from Babylon towards the conclusion of prophecy, there is no record of a Jewish king, such as the prophecy predicts, except our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, in Whom this prediction was fulfilled, when He literally said to His disciples:

"Go ye into the village over against you, and ye shall find an ass tied and a colt with her; loose them and bring them unto me. And if any man say, What do ye? ye shall say to him, The Lord hath need of them. And they went and did as he commanded them."

Such, then, was the prophecy and such the fulfilment. But what was His riding on an ass meant to shew forth but the lowly and humble manner which marked His first Coming? For the second Coming shall be glorious, that of which Daniel speaks unfolding and revealing his vision:

"9. I saw until the thrones were set, and the Ancient of Days did sit. Thousand thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. 13. […]
9:9.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 17

9:9.t: Without Benjamin, the patriarchs went forth; without Paul, the apostles. Neither of them came first, but being summoned by the first, they made greater profit from the arrival of those who came before. There is, he says, grain in Egypt, that is, where there is greater hunger, there is greater plenty. There is much grain in Egypt. Finally, even God the Father says: Out of Egypt I have called my Son. From this seed comes that abundance. For there could not have been a harvest unless the Egyptians had sown the seed beforehand. Therefore, there is grain that no one believed existed before. The patriarchs trade in this grain. And indeed, they brought silver, but the good Joseph gave grain and returned the silver. For Christ is not bought with money, but with grace. Your price is faith. These divine mysteries are bought. However, that unclean donkey carried this grain in the law, but now it is clean in grace.

But how, after not walking openly in Jewry, and retiring into the wilderness, doth He again enter openly? Having quenched their anger by retiring, He cometh to them when they were stilled. Moreover, the multitude which went before and which followed after was sufficient to cast them into an agony; for no sign so much attracted the people as that of Lazarus. And another Evangelist saith, that they strewed their garments under His feet, and that "the whole city was moved"; with so great honor did He enter. And this He did, figuring one prophecy and fulfilling another; and the same act was the beginning of the one and the end of the other. For the, "Rejoice, for thy King cometh unto thee meek," belonged to Him as fulfilling a prophecy, but the sitting upon an ass was the act of one prefiguring a future event, that He was about to have the impure race of the Gentiles subject to Him. ... But what meaneth, "Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion"? […]
