For these things it is not absurd to use the examples of the prophet Zechariah, which run thus: "and it shall be in that day that I will seek to take away all the nations that come against Jerusalem, and I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants in Jerusalem a spirit of grace and of compassion; and they shall look upon me because they danced, and they shall mourn over themselves a mourning as over a beloved one, and they shall grieve with grief as over a firstborn. And in that day the mourning shall be magnified in Jerusalem like the mourning of a pomegranate cut down in the field, and the earth shall mourn by tribes: the tribe of the house of David apart by itself and their women apart by themselves; the tribe of the house of Nathan apart by itself and their women apart by themselves; […]

And it shall be on that day: I will seek to crush all the nations that come against Jerusalem. And I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the spirit of grace and of prayers. LXX: And it shall be on that day: I will seek to take away all the nations that come against Jerusalem; and I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the spirit of grace and of mercy. On that day when the Lord shall shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the Lord will seek to crush all the nations that come against Jerusalem. But he will crush them not unto perdition but unto amendment, so that they may cease to wage war against Jerusalem and begin to be of Jerusalem. For if he created all things out of nothing, he did not make them in order to destroy what he had created, but so that the things that were created might be saved by his mercy. […]

12:10.t: And in what kind of sensation and punishment the wicked are to be, hear from what was said in like manner with reference to this; it is as follows: "Their worm shall not rest, and their fire shall not be quenched;" and then shall they repent, when it profits them not. And what the people of the Jews shall say and do, when they see Him coming in glory, has been thus predicted by Zechariah the prophet: "I will command the four winds to gather the scattered children; I will command the north wind to bring them, and the south wind, that it keep not back. And then in Jerusalem there shall be great lamentation, not the lamentation of mouths or of lips, but the lamentation of the heart; and they shall rend not their garments, but their hearts. Tribe by tribe they shall mourn, and then they shall look on Him whom they have pierced; and they shall say, Why, O Lord, hast Thou made us to err from Thy way? The glory which our fathers blessed, has for us been turned into shame."

We must after all this turn our attention to those scriptures also which forbid our belief in such a resurrection as is held by your Animalists (for I will not call them Spiritualists), that it is either to be assumed as taking place now, as soon as men come to the knowledge of the truth, or else that it is accomplished immediately after their departure from this life... Who has yet beheld Jesus descending from heaven in like manner as the apostles saw Him ascend, according to the appointment of the two angels? [Acts 1:11] Up to the present moment they have not, tribe by tribe, smitten their breasts, looking on Him whom they pierced. [John 19:37; Zechariah 12:10] No one has as yet fallen in with Elias; [Malachi 4:5] no one has as yet escaped from Antichrist; [1 John 4:3] no one has as yet had to bewail the downfall of Babylon. [Revelation 18:2] And is there now anybody who has risen again, except the heretic? […]
12:10.s: On the Resurrection of the Flesh, Chapter 22

12:10.t: Yea, in return for their insults to the Lord who thus prophesied, there has not failed for them lamentation, mourning and wailing. And it was only after our Saviour came, and even until our own time, that all the families of the Jewish nation have suffered pain worthy of wailing and lamentation because God's hand has struck them, delivering their mother-city over to strange nations, laying their Temple low, and driving them from their country, to serve their enemies in a hostile land; wherefore even now every house and every soul is a prey to lamentation. And so the prophecy says, "And family shall mourn by family, the family of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves, and all that follows this."
12:10.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 4

12:10.t: In short, there follows: I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the spirit of grace and of mercy. Of this grace the apostle Paul also writes: The charity of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. And in the above-mentioned volume it is contained: The things that are in heaven, who has searched out? Except that you gave wisdom and sent your Holy Spirit from on high; and so the paths of those who dwell on earth were corrected; and men were taught the things that please you. And in Isaiah the Lord says: I have given my spirit upon you. And again Scripture records of the same: I have given my Spirit upon him. But the word of pouring out shows the sense of largess, as is plain in what we have said: The charity of God has been poured out in your hearts. And in another place, in the person of God: I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh. […]

And they shall look upon me whom they pierced; and they shall mourn him with a mourning as over an only-begotten, and they shall grieve over him, as one is wont to grieve at the death of a firstborn. LXX: And they shall look upon me, because they mocked; and they shall mourn over him a mourning, as over one most dear. And they shall grieve with grief, as over a firstborn. The Hebrew letters daleth and res, that is, d and r, are alike and are distinguished only by a small stroke. From this it comes about that those who read the same word differently translate it now one way, now another. For the sake of understanding let us give one example: And Samuel, it says, was clothed in an ephod bad, that is, in a linen garment; for linen is called bad; hence also linens are called baddim. In place of this Hebrew and Latin expression some wrongly read ephod bar; for bar means either a son, or a sheaf of grain, or chosen, or οὖλος, that is, curly. […]

He commanded them, among other things, to pray as follows: "And forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors." Or [it may be that] he calls his disciples "evil" because in comparison with the divine goodness, every creature is judged to be evil, as the Lord says, "No one is good except God alone." It is only by participation in the divine goodness that a rational creature is recognized as being capable of becoming good. Hence the Lord also bears witness by a benevolent promise that your heavenly Father will "give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him." This is to the point that those who of themselves are evil can become good through receiving the gift of the Spirit. He pledged that his good Spirit would be given by the Father to those asking for him, because whether we desire to secure faith, hope and charity, or any other heavenly goods at all, they are not bestowed upon us otherwise than by the gift of the Holy Spirit. […]

12:11.t: On that day there shall be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning of Adadremmon in the plain of Megiddo. And the land shall mourn, families and families apart; the families of the house of David apart, and the women — or wives —, of them apart — for the Hebrew word nese, that is, γυναῖκες, signifies both —, the families of the house of Nathan apart, and their women apart, the families of the house of Levi apart and their women apart, the families of Shimei apart and their women apart. All the remaining families, families and families apart and their women apart. LXX: On that day there shall be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning for the pomegranate that is cut down in the plain, and the land shall mourn by tribes and tribes; […]

Let us say also that according to the LXX it is called ῥοῶν, not a single tree of pomegranates, that is, of the Punic apple, but a place planted with these trees, of which, according to the spiritual understanding, the bridegroom says in the Song of Songs: I went down to see in the produce of the torrent whether the vine had flowered, whether the pomegranates had flowered. For the Savior went down to the torrent of this world and its turbid waters, from which Elijah too, in a type of him, is described as having drunk, so that after the flowers of the vine and of the pomegranate he might receive the fruit of both, and, making his Church drunk, might hear from her: You shall give me to drink of the perfumer's wine, of the wine of my pomegranates. A drink of this kind not only drives away the heats of the stomach, but is also said to heal a corrupted belly and to benefit the other inner organs. For nothing is more beautiful than this fruit; […]

12:12.t: And as they kept silence, I went on: "[The Scripture], speaking by David about this Christ, my friends, said no longer that 'in His seed' the nations should be blessed, but 'in Him.' So it is here: 'His name shall rise up for ever above the sun; and in Him shall all nations be blessed.' But if all nations are blessed in Christ, and we of all nations believe in Him, then He is indeed the Christ, and we are those blessed by Him. God formerly gave the sun as an object of worship, as it is written, but no one ever was seen to endure death on account of his faith in the sun; but for the name of Jesus you may see men of every nation who have endured and do endure all sufferings, rather than deny Him. For the word of His truth and wisdom is more ardent and more light-giving than the rays of the sun, and sinks down into the depths of heart and mind. Hence also the Scripture said, 'His name shall rise up above the sun.' And again, Zechariah says, 'His name is the East.' […]

Josiah also was persecuted as Jesus was persecuted. Josiah was persecuted, and Pharaoh the Lame slew Him; and Jesus was persecuted, and the people that were made lame by their sins slew Him. Josiah cleansed the land of Israel from uncleanness; and Jesus cleansed and caused to pass away uncleanness from all the earth. Josiah hallowed and glorified the name of his God; and Jesus said:—I have glorified and will glorify (His Name). Josiah because of the iniquity of Israel rent his clothes; and Jesus because of the iniquity of the people rent the vail of the Holy Temple. Josiah said:—Great is the wrath that shall come upon this people; and Jesus said:—There shall come wrath upon this people, and they shall fall by the edge of the sword. Josiah cast out uncleanness from the Holy Temple; and Jesus cast out the unclean traders from His Father’s house. For Josiah the daughters of Israel mourned and wailed, as Jeremiah said:—O daughters of Israel, weep for Josiah; […]

And what follows: The families and families shall mourn, or tribes and tribes, apart: the families of the house of David apart, and the wives or the women of them apart; this signifies that in a time of tribulation and grief we ought not to be given over to marriage and the work of wedlock. Hence also in Joel, when the captivity was near, it is said to the Jews: Let the bridegroom go forth from his chamber, and the bride from her bridal room. And when the flood was impending, Noah is commanded: Enter into the ark, you and your sons, and your wife, and the wives of your sons. And afterwards, when the flood was over, it is said to him: Go out, you and your wife, and your sons, and their wives, so that those who had been separated in the ark while the peril hung over them, once restored to the world, might devote themselves to begetting and to children. […]

12:14.t: He was silent about the remaining tribes, which have no privilege of dignity. But in saying: All the remaining tribes, tribes and tribes apart, and their wives apart, he includes them all without a name.

13:1.t: On that day there shall be a fountain open to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for the washing of the sinner and of the menstruous woman. LXX: On that day every place shall be opened in the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, both for transformation and for sprinkling. Of this fountain, which goes forth from the house of David, it is written also in the prophet Ezekiel that a fountain bursts forth in the house of the Lord and grows into a river, which is called the water of remission and pardon, and goes on to the wilderness and to the sea which is now called the Dead Sea, and gives life to all the fish, and on either bank of the river trees of various kinds rise up, always abounding with new fruits month by month. […]

13:2.t: Let us see, then, the necessity of literary erudition; let us reflect that partly it cannot be admitted, partly cannot be avoided. Learning literature is allowable for believers, rather than teaching; for the principle of learning and teaching is different. If a believer teaches literature, while he teaches doubtless he commends, while he delivers he affirms, while he recalls he bears testimony to, the praise of idols interspersed therein. He seals the gods themselves with this name [of gods], whereas the law, as we have said, prohibits "the names of gods to be pronounced" and this name [of God] to be conferred on vanity. Hence the devil gets people's early faith built up from the beginnings of erudition. Inquire whether he who catechizes about idols commits idolatry. But when a believer learns these things, if he is already capable of understanding what idolatry is, he neither receives nor allows them; much more if he is not yet capable. […]

And it shall be on that day, says the Lord of hosts, I will destroy the names of the idols from the land, and they shall be remembered no more; and the prophets and the unclean spirit I will take away from the land. LXX: And it shall be on that day, says the Lord Sabaoth, I will destroy the names of the idols from the land, and there shall be no more remembrance of them; and the false prophets and the unclean spirit I will take away from the land. On that day, which he mentions so often, all idols shall be taken away from the land: whether those idols of which the psalmist says: The images of the nations are silver and gold, the works of men's hands, so that there may be no other religion but only that of the Christian name, and of which it is written in the prophet: Howl, you carved images in Jerusalem and in Samaria. For as I have done to Samaria and to her carved images, so will I do to Jerusalem and to her idols; […]

Hermes Trismegistus lamented these vain, deceptive, pernicious, sacrilegious things because he foresaw that the time was coming when they would be abolished. He was impudent in his grief as imprudent in his prophecy, since the Holy Spirit had made no revelation to him as to the holy prophets, who exultantly proclaimed their inspired visions: "Shall a man make gods to himself, and they are no gods?" and again, "And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord of hosts, that I will destroy the names of the idols out of the earth, and they shall be remembered no more." It is relevant to recall that holy Isaiah uttered a particular prophecy concerning Egypt: "And the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst thereof," and the rest.

13:3.t: And it shall be, when anyone prophesies any more, his father and his mother, who begot him, shall say to him: You shall not live, because you have spoken a lie in the name of the Lord; and his father and his mother, who begot him, shall pierce him when he prophesies. LXX: And it shall be, if a man prophesies any more, his father and his mother, who begot him, shall say to him: You shall not live, because you have spoken a lie in the name of the Lord; and his father and his mother who begot him shall fetter him when he prophesies. When the names of the idols have been taken away from the land, and the false prophets, and the unclean spirit that spoke in them, if anyone wishes to try any more and to prophesy something in the person of the Lord, at once his father and mother will forget that they are parents, so as to hold fast to the service of God, and they will pronounce the sentence of death against their son; […]

13:4.t: And it shall be on that day, the prophets shall be confounded, each one by his vision when he has prophesied, nor shall they be covered with a cloak of sackcloth in order to lie. But he shall say: I am not a prophet, I am a man, a tiller of the ground, for Adam has been my example from my youth. And it shall be said to him: What are these wounds in the middle of your hands? And he shall say: With these I was wounded in the house of those who loved me. LXX: And it shall be on that day, the prophets shall be confounded, each one by his vision when he has prophesied, and they shall put on a skin of haircloth because they have lied; and he shall say: I am not a prophet, for a man begot me from my youth. And I will say to him: What are these wounds in the middle of your hands? And he shall say: Those with which I was struck in the house of the one who loved me. […]

What is written, Nor shall they be covered with a cloak of sackcloth in order to lie, the Hebrews expound thus: and they shall not be filled with the demonic spirit, those whom we read of in Isaiah as τριχιῶντας, that is, hairy ones, lest on this occasion of a feigned habit they belie the utterances of God within them, or deny God. For Chaesu can be interpreted both 'they shall lie' and 'they shall deny'.

13:5.t: Therefore this false prophet too will by no means take up the prophetic habit, lest under another's clothing and covering he deceive all the simple, but rather he will cleave the earth with the ploughshare and, given over to farming, will prove himself a man, and subject to the sentence of God, who spoke to Adam: Cursed is the ground in your work; in toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life; thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the plants of the earth; and in the sweat of your face you shall eat bread.

Again, in Zechariah thirteen it is said: I am a husbandman, for Adam has been my example from my youth; Gloss: "That I may eat my bread in the sweat of my face, while he showed himself born for this, that in the sweat of his face he might eat bread"; but this most befits one who needs bread and can bear labor and sweat; and such is the able-bodied poor person: therefore he is bound to labor bodily.
13:5.s: Disputed Questions on Evangelical Perfection, Question 2

13:6.t: And when he has shown that he was born for this, to eat his bread in the sweat of his face, another will question him and say: What do these wounds mean, and these gashes that are in the middle of your hands? And the sense is: Why do you cling to the gibbet? Why are your hands pierced with nails? What have you committed, that you should be subjected to this penalty and torment? And he will answer and say: These gashes and these wounds I received, condemned by the judgment of my parents and of those who did not hate me but loved me. And truth will prevail so far, once falsehood has been put to flight, that even he who has been punished for his own fault confesses that he has suffered justly.

14:5.t: Christ, then, was crucified for us; he was judged in the night, when it was cold, and therefore a fire of coal was laid. He was crucified in the third hour, and "from the sixth hour there was darkness until the ninth hour," but from the ninth hour there was light again. Are these details written down? Let us inquire. Zechariah says, "And it shall come to pass in that day, and there shall be no light but cold and frost through one day (the cold on account of which Peter warmed himself), and that day shall be known to the Lord." (What? Did he not know the other days? There are many days, but "this is the day [of the Lord's patience] the Lord has made.")6 "And that day shall be known to the Lord, and not day nor night." What dark saying does the prophet utter? That day is neither day nor night. What then shall we call it? The gospel interprets it, telling of the event. It was not day, for the sun did not shine without interruption from rising to setting, but from the sixth hour to the ninth there was darkness. […]

Yet learn that the Son knows the day of judgment. We read in Zechariah: "And the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with him. In that day there shall not be light but cold and frost, and it shall be one day, and that day is known to the Lord." This day, then, was known unto the Lord, who shall come with his saints to enlighten us by his second advent. But let us continue the point that we have commenced concerning the Spirit: "He shall glorify me." So then the Spirit glorifies the Son, as the Father also glorifies him, but the Son of God also glorifies the Spirit, as we said. He then is not weak who is the cause of the mutual glory through the unity of the eternal light, nor is he inferior to the Spirit, of whom this is true that he is glorified by the Spirit.

Their flesh shall waste away as they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall flow out of their sockets, and their tongue shall waste away in their mouth. What the nations that shall fight against the city of the Lord are to suffer, the present scripture testifies. They shall stand, he says, upon their feet, and their flesh shall waste away and flow off, and their eyes shall rot and fall out of their sockets; the boastful tongue, which used to blaspheme the people of God, shall be dissolved into corruption and rot within the rampart of the teeth. […]

14:13.t: On that day there shall be a great tumult from the Lord among them, and a man shall seize the hand of his neighbor, and his hand shall be locked upon the hand of his neighbor. But Judah too shall fight against Jerusalem, and the riches of all the nations round about shall be gathered together, gold and silver, and garments in great abundance. LXX: And it shall be on that day, a great stupor from the Lord upon them, and each one shall seize the hand of his neighbor, and his hand shall cling to the hand of his neighbor. And Judah shall be made ready in Jerusalem, and shall gather the strength of all the peoples round about, gold, silver, and garments exceedingly many. When these wonders have been accomplished, so that the flesh of the enemies flows away, their eyes waste, and the tongue rots in the mouth of the blasphemers, then there shall be a great tumult, or stupor, among them; […]

14:15.t: And so shall be the ruin of the horse, and of the mule and of the camel, and of the ass, and of all the beasts that shall be in those camps, like this ruin. LXX: And this shall be the ruin of the horses and of the mules and of the camels and of the asses, and of all the beasts that shall be in those camps, according to this ruin. These things too the Jews contend are to be fulfilled carnally under their ἠλειμμένῳ (anointed one). Great indeed is the strength of the Lord, that in the camps of the enemies the horses and mules, camels and asses, and all their beasts should fall, just as the men had fallen. A great triumph, a glorious victory, that brute animals should be overcome with God fighting! Let us say, therefore, according to the tropology we have begun, that all the evil things which formerly fought against the Church fall for this reason, that good things may suddenly rise up. […]

14:16.t:
[Passage quoted, Zech. xiv. 16-19.]

This passage clearly implies the calling of all the Gentiles, if we only regard the sense of what is said about Jerusalem and the tabernacle, to which I will give the proper interpretation in its right place.
14:16.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 1

14:16.t: And if they say that they were chosen out to act as priests and to offer worship to God, it can be shewn that the Word promised that He would give to the Gentiles an equal share in His service, when He said: "Render to the Lord, O ye kindreds of the nations, render to the Lord glory and honour: bring sacrifices and come into his courts." To which the oracle in Isaiah may be conjoined, which says: "There shall be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt . . . and the Egyptians will know the Lord. And they shall do sacrifice, and say prayers to the Lord, and offer." And in this you will understand that it is prophesied that an altar will be built to the Lord away from Jerusalem in Egypt, and that the Egyptians will there offer sacrifice, say prayers and give gifts to the Lord. Yes, and not only in Egypt, but in the true Jerusalem itself, whatever it is thought to be, all the nations, and the Egyptians forsooth, the most superstitious of them all, are invited to keep the Feast of Tabernacles, as a feast of the heart.
14:16.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

14:16.t: And it was when our Lord Jesus, the Christ of God, had visited the olive-grove over against Jerusalem, since the words of the prophecy were fulfilled which said, "His feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives opposite to Jerusalem," that is, the life of holiness having been established throughout all the world, that all the nations, according to the prophecy, kept the Feast of Tabernacles together in every place to the God of the prophets, and the Egyptians from that time recognizing God erected tents in every town and country place, which mean the local Christian Churches. For the power of our Saviour Jesus Christ has pegged them far better than Moses' tents through the whole world, so that every race of men and all the Gentiles may keep their Feast of Tabernacles to Almighty God.
14:16.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 4

14:16.t: And all who are left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem shall go up from year to year to worship the king, the Lord of hosts, and to celebrate the feast of tabernacles. LXX: And it shall be, whoever are left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem shall go up every year to worship the king, the Lord Almighty, and to celebrate the feast of tabernacles. All, he says, who are left of the nations that came against Jerusalem shall go up every year to worship the king, the Lord of hosts, and to celebrate the feast of tabernacles. These things too the Jews, with empty hope, promise will come to pass in the kingdom of a thousand years. The origin of this solemnity is as follows. […]

14:17.t: And it shall be that whoever of the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, upon them there shall be no rain. LXX: And it shall be that whoever of the families of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, these also shall be added to those. Where the Seventy translated, and these also shall be added to those, in the Hebrew is written ulo alehem eie gesem, which Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion have likewise interpreted: And upon them there shall be no rain. The Church of the Lord Jesus is called the heavenly Jerusalem, of which the Apostle writes: But the Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all, and: You have come to Mount Zion, and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. And this Jerusalem is not set in low places, but on a lofty mountain, of which the Savior speaks: A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden. […]

14:18.t: And if the families of Egypt do not go up and do not come, neither shall it be upon them; but there shall be the ruin with which the Lord will strike all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the solemnity of tabernacles. This shall be the sin of Egypt, and this the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the festival of tabernacles. LXX: But if the tribe of Egypt does not go up, nor come there, upon them also shall be the ruin with which the Lord will strike all the nations that did not go up to keep the solemnity of the scenopegia. This shall be the sin of Egypt, and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the solemnity of the scenopegia. Whoever is an Egyptian, or of the other nations, as long as he remains an Egyptian and a heathen, will not go up into Jerusalem; and because he cannot go up, nor lift his step to the heights, therefore upon him there shall be no rain of the Lord's blessing.

14:19.t: And this shall be the greatest sin for the Egyptian, the Assyrian, the Chaldean, the Syrian, the Moabite and the Ammonite, if they are unwilling to go out from their lands and go up to Jerusalem, so that through the tabernacles they may pass into Jerusalem and find an eternal house, and cease to be men of other nations, and become Israelites in whom there is no guile. All these things, which we touch on in brief speech, the Jews and our judaizers, or rather not ours, since they are judaizers, hope will come to pass bodily, promising themselves, of course, both circumcision and marriages in the reign of a thousand years, so that the curse which is written may not be fulfilled in them: Cursed is the barren woman who does not bear seed in Israel, and: Blessed is he who has seed in Zion and household members in Jerusalem. If this is true, all the virgins whom the kingdom of a thousand years finds will lie under the curse and perpetual barrenness, or else they will marry so as to escape the curse.

14:20.t: On that day what is upon the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord; and the cauldrons in the house of the Lord shall be like bowls before the altar. And every cauldron in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be sanctified to the Lord of hosts. LXX: On that day what is upon the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord Almighty; and the cauldrons that are in the house of the Lord shall be like bowls before the house of the altar. And every cauldron in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holy to the Lord Almighty. The Hebrew word mesuloth Aquila and Theodotion interpreted as βυθὸν, that is, depth; Symmachus as περίπατον σύσκιον, that is, a shady walk. The Seventy alone translated χάλινον, that is, bridle, and we too have followed them in this place, so as not to seem to bring something new into a well-known question. […]

Let us pass on to the cauldrons, which are to be in the house of the Lord like the bowls of the altar. For every cauldron in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be sanctified to the Lord Almighty. Let them love bronze cauldrons who loved the pots of Egypt and the meat, and the melons and the garlic, and the onions and the cucumbers. Let us turn the Jewish cauldrons, in which the flesh of the victims was cooked, into bowls of spices before the altar of the Lord, of which the bride says to the bridegroom: My kinsman has gone down into my garden, to the bowls of spices, to feed in the gardens and to gather lilies. The garden and paradise into which the bridegroom goes down to the bride is the reading of the holy scriptures, from which he plucks lilies and violets and roses and various spices, to fill the bowls of believing souls and to pour out libations to the Lord from them. […]

14:21.t: And all these shall come sacrificing, and taking from them, and they shall cook in them; and there shall no longer be a merchant in the house of the Lord of hosts on that day. LXX: And all who sacrifice shall come and shall take from them, and they shall cook in them; and there shall no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord Almighty on that day. In place of Canaanite, Aquila translated merchant, and we too have followed him in this place. When the cauldrons have been turned into bowls, all the nations round about, or those who are left of all the nations, will come sacrificing, and will take the cauldrons and cook in them the flesh of the victims, so that they may not eat the flesh of the lamb raw, but, all the juice of the meat having been boiled away, what has been prepared by fire may remain for eating. What the bowls before the altar of the Lord are, into which the Israelite cauldrons are turned, we have both said above and shall now say in part. […]
